title: What does ConfidentialMPTConvert do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of ConfidentialMPTConvert and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, ConfidentialMPTConvert moves an MPT holder's public balance into confidential form. [1]

The reference requires cryptographic commitments and proofs to keep balances consistent without publishing the hidden amount in the ordinary way. Conversion stays within the same issuance rather than exchanging one currency for another. A wallet needs the supported confidentiality machinery as well as an eligible MPT; hiding an amount is not the same as hiding every transaction participant. [1]

The ConfidentialMPTConvert reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using ConfidentialMPTConvert, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
